instructions.english_purpose: Please confirm or edit the suggested Spanish term for each English glossary entry. The Spanish suggestions are starting points, not approved translations.
english_items: Read the English term, definition or meaning, example, and ‘Why it matters’ note before deciding.
Keep every numeric threshold and distinction exact, including ≤ 2%, ≤ 1%, ≤ 0.1%, the 100+ daily-intercessor goal, and the CPM measures.

Use standard Spanish spelling and script. Keep Doxa.Life and DOXA unchanged. Retain UPG, UUPG, and CPM alongside the Spanish phrase unless you recommend a stable Spanish acronym and explain it in Notes.

For biblical phrases, use the wording of the Bible translation most commonly used by your local church or Assemblies of God/Pentecostal community—not merely your personal preference. Record its exact title, abbreviation, edition, and year below. If local communities commonly use more than one translation, list the primary one first and note the others.
Check that related terms form a coherent family, especially engage / engaged / engagement / unengaged / under-engaged / fruitful engagement.
Choose Approve if the suggested Spanish term is accurate, natural in Spanish evangelical and missional usage, and suitable for both prose and interface labels.
Choose Edit if you prefer another term. Write the complete preferred term in the Final Spanish term field; do not merely describe the change.
instructions.local_purpose: Confirme o modifique el término sugerido en español para cada entrada del glosario inglés. Las sugerencias son puntos de partida, no traducciones aprobadas.
local_items: Lea el término inglés, la definición o significado, el ejemplo y la nota «Por qué importa» antes de decidir.
Mantenga exactos todos los umbrales y distinciones numéricas, incluidos ≤ 2 %, ≤ 1 %, ≤ 0,1 %, la meta de más de 100 intercesores diarios y las medidas de CPM.

Use la ortografía y los signos diacríticos correctos del español. Mantenga Doxa.Life y DOXA sin cambios. Conserve UPG, UUPG y CPM junto a la expresión española salvo que recomiende una sigla española estable y la explique en Notas.

Para las expresiones bíblicas, use la redacción de la traducción de la Biblia más utilizada por su iglesia local o comunidad de las Asambleas de Dios/pentecostal. Anote el título exacto, la abreviatura, la edición y el año.
Compruebe que los términos relacionados formen una familia coherente, especialmente engage / engaged / engagement / unengaged / under-engaged / fruitful engagement.
Marque Aprobar si el término sugerido es exacto, natural en el uso evangélico y misionológico y sirve para texto y etiquetas de interfaz.
Marque Modificar si prefiere otro término. Escriba el término completo en el campo Término final en español; no describa solamente el cambio.

People group.note: Asked whether "grupo de personas" should stay, the reviewer answered "grupo étnico". It carries the ethnolinguistic sense more tightly and is the base the Spanish acronyms build on: "if we will use the term 'grupo étnico' instead of 'grupo de personas', we can replace [PNANC] for 'GENANC'". The marketing site's Definitions draft still reads "pueblo étnico"; the reviewed glossary supersedes it.

Unreached people group (UPG).note: The reviewer's policy is a Spanish acronym in place of the English one, but the reviewed glossary gives none for UPG, so none is set. The marketing Definitions draft abbreviated it PNA (pueblo étnico no alcanzado), which predates the switch to grupo étnico.

Unengaged (people group).note: Asked to review "no comprometido" because it can sound as if the group itself lacks commitment, the reviewer kept it: "'comprometido' is the right word to engage someone with responsibility and commitment. 'Involucramiento' means to involve someone in a project or an action. For that reason, 'comprometido' is a correct term." The marketing Definitions draft's "sin compromiso" and "grupo desvinculado" are superseded. Lowercase in running text: "In Spanish, 'Unengaged or Unreached' go as lowercase letters."

Unengaged unreached people group (UUPG).value: grupo étnico no alcanzado no comprometido (GENANC)
Unengaged unreached people group (UUPG).note: A Spanish acronym replaces UUPG everywhere: "I have used a Spanish abbreviation instead of the English one … Please add this where all the UUPG are in the English version." The reviewer first worked with PNANC (pueblo no alcanzado no comprometido) on the marketing site, then, once grupo étnico was chosen, offered "'GENANC' (grupo étnico no alcanzado no comprometido) or 'GNANC' (grupo no alcanzado no comprometido)"; the reviewed glossary uses GENANC throughout ("Busca un GENANC", "2.085 GENANC"). As a technical term or acronym expansion use the form without "y"; in descriptive prose "grupo étnico no alcanzado y no comprometido" reads more naturally.

Under-engaged (people group).note: Conveys that work has begun but is insufficient in scale, not that the people are indifferent, and keeps the comprometido family together. The marketing form's worked example ("pocos comprometidos" → "pocos alcanzados") is not followed; the reviewed glossary keeps "poco comprometido".

Frontier people (group).note: The reviewed glossary headword; its Definitions draft reads "grupo étnico fronterizo" in full. For the homepage statistic label the reviewer corrected "gente de la frontera" to "gente fronteriza".

Engagement / engaged (people group).note: Asked to consider "compromiso" carefully because it can blur engagement as technical resident ministry with commitment as attitude, the reviewer confirmed it: "'comprometido' is the right word to engage someone with responsibility and commitment. 'Involucramiento' means to involve someone in a project or an action." The verb is "comprometer" ("Comprometer a todos los grupos étnicos no comprometidos para 2033"); "involucrar" and "participación" from the earlier marketing drafts are superseded.

Fruitful engagement.note: Word order corrected by the reviewer on the homepage: "'Fructífero compromiso' replace with 'Compromiso fructífero'".

Church-planting movement (CPM).note: Spanish acronym MPI, following the reviewer's policy of replacing English acronyms; the reviewed glossary uses MPI in both the CPM entry and the unengaged definition.

Indigenous church.note: "Autóctona" means locally rooted and self-governing; the marketing Vision-page draft's "iglesia indígena" is superseded by the reviewed glossary.

The five \"selfs\" (of an indigenous chu.value: los cinco «auto» de una iglesia autóctona
The five \"selfs\" (of an indigenous chu.note: The five per the reviewed glossary: autogobierno, autosustento, autopropagación, autoteologización y automisionología. The marketing Definitions draft's variants (autosostenimiento, automisión) are superseded.

Cross-cultural workers.note: "Obreros" is the reviewed glossary's word ("Los obreros transculturales son residentes"); the marketing Vision-page draft reads "trabajadores transculturales".

Pioneer work.note: The reviewed glossary headword; the marketing Definitions draft reads "la obra pionera".

Heart language.note: The reviewed glossary headword; its quoted Definitions text reads "idioma del corazón".

Nonresident partners.note: The marketing Definitions draft reads "socios no residentes"; the reviewed glossary settles on "asociados", matching "misioneros asociados a DOXA" and "Asociarse" for Partner.

Broader engagement (components).value: componentes de un compromiso más amplio
Broader engagement (components).note: Asked whether "componentes de mayor compromiso" could be smoothed, the reviewer chose "componentes de un compromiso más amplio", which maps "broader engagement" directly. The marketing Definitions draft's "una participación más amplia" is superseded.

suggested_terms.Daily prayer (for a people group): oración diaria (por un grupo étnico específico)

Daily prayer guide / daily prayer points.value: guía diaria de oración / motivos diarios de oración
Daily prayer guide / daily prayer points.note: The reviewed glossary headword. Its own example still quotes the site's "puntos de oración diarios" and "Tu guía de oración diaria", and on the marketing form the reviewer rendered daily prayer points as "pedidos de oración" ("Reciba diariamente pedidos de oración").

Lord of the harvest.note: The reviewed glossary's wording, which matches the NVI (Mateo 9:38); Reina-Valera 1960 reads "Señor de la mies", and the glossary's own gloss keeps that word ("mies = personas listas para responder"). The reviewer did not record which Bible translation their community uses.

Pray, give, and send.note: In the triad "dar" stays ("orando, dando y preparando el camino"); as a standalone footer label the reviewer replaced "DAR" with "DONAR", and the noun is "donaciones" ("Asociarse mediante la oración, las donaciones y el envío").

Sending agency / sending agencies.note: World Assemblies of God Fellowship in the example is "Fraternidad Mundial de las Asambleas de Dios (FMAD)": "WAGF, the Spanish translation is 'FMAD'".

Priority — \"Engage every Unengaged Peop.value: Prioridad: «Comprometer a todos los grupos étnicos no comprometidos para el año 2033»
Priority — \"Engage every Unengaged Peop.note: "Comprometer" follows the reviewer's compromiso family; the marketing Vision-page draft's "Involucrar" is superseded. The reviewed glossary writes the year as 2033 throughout (Visión 2033, para el año 2033); the marketing form's "EL 2.033" for the homepage headline is not followed. The reviewer's dot-for-thousands rule applies to counts (2.085, 20.000, 3.900 millones).

Every tribe, tongue, people, and nation.value: cada tribu, lengua, pueblo y nación
Every tribe, tongue, people, and nation.note: The reviewed glossary keeps the English order of the four nouns and asks to align with the established Bible translation; the reviewer's Vision-page draft quotes Apocalipsis 7:9 as "todas las naciones y familias y pueblos y lenguas".
